The must-sees

  • Swakopmund Jetty

    Waterfront · 1912

    Work began in 1912 to replace a wooden jetty but stopped with the First World War. Restored in the 2000s, it is now a promenade out over the surf.

    Look for: Just north, the Mole still curves out from the shore, now enclosing a sheltered beach of sand where ships were meant to tie up.

  • Swakopmund Lighthouse

    Landmark · 1903

    First lit in 1903, it was raised to 21 metres in 1910. It still works and is the town’s symbol.

    Look for: Next door stands State House, built as the colonial district court and now a holiday residence of Namibia’s president.

  • Woermannhaus

    Building · 1906

    Built for the Woermann shipping line, it has a half-timbered courtyard and the Damara Tower. The tower once guided ships and now gives views over the town and dunes.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Swakopmund and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Swakopmund passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
